caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:pfc-7
attempts.entry_title: Attention and decision computations across prefrontal cortex (Hunt, Malalasekera et al. 2018)
attempts.summary: The paper's main findings held up in this data: spatial attention in DLPFC, stimulus identity and attended value in OFC, and accept/reject and left/right value in ACC at cue 1, the OFC comparison of attended against stored value, and the ACC belief-confirmation signal that predicts reaction time. Some held under only a few of the readings tried, such as the ACC action ramp and OFC leading in value-difference neurons. Figure 8's action-value neurons in ACC and DLPFC pass their tests, but their fractions do not both fall near the paper's 18%, a gap the attempt puts down to permutation noise. Among minor claims, the supplementary latency order and equal cue weights in monkey M did not reproduce.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Hunt, Malalasekera et al. (2018) on CRCNS data set pfc-7, which holds the behaviour of two macaques in an information sampling task and single units from ACC, DLPFC and OFC. It covers the behaviour, the representational similarity analysis at cue 1, the value comparison subspaces in OFC, the belief confirmation and action subspaces in ACC, and the single-neuron analyses, all from the data set's preprocessed units and behavioural files.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hunt, Malalasekera et al. (2018) from CRCNS pfc-7

outcomes.statement: Behaviour comes from 25 sessions of monkey F and 32 of monkey M, 9,863 trials for F and 14,251 for M.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 1 legend
outcomes.quote: Regression models were fit to all trials, collapsed across sessions (n=14,251 trials (subject M), n=9,863 trials (subject F))
outcomes.notes: The behavioural files hold 25 sessions of Frank (F) and 32 of Miles (M), with 9863 and 14251 completed option and attribute trials (trial errors 0 and 6 only), the paper's counts under reading (a). Without trials of equal expected value (reading c) there are 9479 and 13691. Aborted trials (reading b) can be counted only from the unit files, for the 24 and 29 sessions with units (10688 and 14391 trials there).
deviations: Reading (b) could be counted only for sessions with units, as the behavioural files hold completed trials only.

outcomes.statement: After excluding units with mean firing rate below 1 Hz (9 ACC, 21 DLPFC, 12 OFC), the analyses use 189 ACC, 135 DLPFC and 183 OFC neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraph 1; Online Methods, Neuronal Recordings, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: We excluded neurons with an average firing rate of <1Hz from further analysis (9 units in ACC, 21 in DLPFC, 12 in OFC; n reported in main text are after these units have been removed)
outcomes.notes: With the average_firing_rate of other_data/all_units_info.mat, the rate every figure script of the paper uses to select units (Fig4_RSA.m and others), 189 ACC, 135 DLPFC and 183 OFC units are at or above 1 Hz, with 9, 21 and 12 excluded, the paper's numbers. The claims file's readings do not give them; the whole-session rate (from OverallSpikeCodes, equal to the stored session mean within 0.004 Hz) gives 190, 136 and 182, the rate from trial start to response 186, 137 and 179. The data set holds 198 ACC, 156 DLPFC and 195 OFC units over 24 F and 29 M sessions, the totals and session counts of Supplementary Table 1 as the claims file gives them. Session by session the table agrees with the data in all 53 sessions and three areas when every unit is counted, and in 26 of 53 when units below 1 Hz are left out, so it counts all units although its caption says units above 1 Hz. The scripts also drop unit 87 (DLPFC, 4.8 Hz) as a bad cell, so the paper's DLPFC analyses, and these, use 134 units.
deviations: The rate is the stored average_firing_rate that the paper's scripts use, a third reading besides the claims file's two; how it was computed is not documented in the data set.

outcomes.statement: Monkeys F and M chose the option with the higher expected value on 76.6% and 79.8% of trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 2; Figure 1b
outcomes.quote: They chose the option with higher expected value on 76.6% and 79.8% of trials (monkeys F (n=25 sessions) and M (n=32 sessions) respectively)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), ties left out, gives 75.71% (F) and 79.01% (M); reading (b) 72.77% and 75.90%. InfoGathering_Behaviour.m counts the 384 and 560 tied trials as correct, which gives 76.66% and 79.83%, the paper's numbers.

outcomes.statement: Monkeys F and M chose before seeing all four cues on 85.5% and 71.4% of trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: subjects chose before all four cues had been evaluated on 85.5%/71.4% of trials (subjects F/M respectively)
outcomes.notes: With the count of pictures corrected for a joystick movement made before the last picture was fixated (num_pics_viewedprezero of InfoGathering_Behaviour.m), F chose before all four cues on 85.52% and M on 71.43% of trials. The raw count of fixated pictures gives 54.23% and 42.56%, and pictures fixated for more than 250 ms 95.59% and 92.25%, both outside the tolerance, so the outcome rests on the definition of a cue "evaluated", which the paper does not give. The claim has no criterion; a question asks a reader whether the claims file should name the readings (questions/hunt-2018.yaml).
deviations: Assumed, as the claims file gives no method and the paper does not define "evaluated" (Results, paragraph 2, "subjects chose before all four cues had been evaluated"). The count is the script's (InfoGathering_Behaviour.m, out.earlychoices), with its joystick threshold and smoothing, the only one of the three counts that the paper's own code computes for this number.

outcomes.statement: Judged by the pictures observed, choice accuracy was 86.3% for monkey F and 87.4% for monkey M.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Choice accuracy based upon the pictures observed ... was substantially higher (86.3% and 87.4% for monkey F and M respectively)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) gives 86.00% (F) and 87.75% (M), reading (b) 79.88% and 82.26%, reading (c) 89.17% and 89.20%, the script's own measure (unseen at 0.5, ties counted correct) 87.80% and 89.48%. Counting every fixated picture as seen gives 79.14% and 81.35% under reading (a).
deviations: Which pictures count as observed is taken from InfoGathering_Behaviour.m (accuracy_seen) as those fixated before the joystick moved, dropping a last picture fixated for 250 ms or less.

outcomes.statement: In logistic regressions of choice, both monkeys weighted reward probability and magnitude about equally and used all four viewed cues, with a slight upweighting of the antepenultimate (n-2) cue, and both showed a small bias towards choosing the second side on option trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 1A and 1B
outcomes.quote: Both subjects use all four cues to guide their choices, with a slight upweighting of the antepenultimate cue ... both subjects show a small but significant bias towards choosing the second side on option trials
outcomes.notes: Model A gives positive picture weights with p < 0.05 for all four positions in both monkeys and both scales. The first-side term on option trials is negative in both (F b = -0.467, p = 1.5e-07; M b = -1.220, p = 2.7e-54). Probability and magnitude weights are both positive, but in M they are not approximately equal under either reading (option ratio 1.11, attribute 1.13; 95% CIs do not overlap; Wald p = 1.1e-06 and 4.1e-07); with true values the M ratios are 1.11 and 1.15. In F the CIs overlap on both trial types (Wald p = 0.53 and 0.002 with seen values). The n-2 weight is below the n-1 weight (ranks F 1.186 against 1.347, M 1.161 against 1.229) and above the final weight (0.270 and 0.284), so the legend's slight upweighting of the antepenultimate cue is not seen against n-1. The claims file's reading (b) of model A, raw values signed by side, carries a side offset (final weight in F 0.270 with ranks, 2.156 with raw values); both codings pass, and a question asks a reader whether the reading should centre the values (questions/hunt-2018.yaml).
deviations: Model B uses the seen values (unseen at 0.5, magnitudes shifted by -0.05) as InfoGathering_Behaviour.m does; the true values are shown too.

outcomes.statement: Choices were more often optimal on trials where 2 pictures were viewed than on trials with 3 or 4, because trials ended early when the first two cues gave a larger value difference.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 1C and 1D
outcomes.quote: Surprisingly, choice accuracy was also higher on trials where subjects sampled fewer pieces of information ( Fig. S1c ). This was because such trials were associated with a higher value difference, and so subjects terminated these trials more quickly ( Fig. S1d ).
outcomes.notes: A reader's answer (questions/hunt-2018.yaml) amended the criterion to allow two measures of accuracy, (A) the higher true expected value and (B) the higher expected value of the pictures observed, under the readings of choice-accuracy-observed, with trials pooled over sessions. The first run tested (A) only and gave not_reproduced. Under (B), with the script's count of pictures, accuracy on 2-picture trials is the highest in both monkeys under all four readings, under reading (a) F 90.24% against 82.67% and 79.81% on 3 and 4 pictures, M 94.62% against 85.98% and 81.70%. Under (A) it is not (F 74.96% against 76.10% and 79.62%; M 78.83% against 78.79% and 81.51%). The mean value difference is largest on 2-picture trials in both monkeys under both readings (true expected values F 0.266, 0.229, 0.219; M 0.271, 0.240, 0.228). The script's mean over sessions, the variant, gives the same order as (B) (F 90.19%, 82.63%, 82.27%; M 93.65%, 85.20%, 83.69%).
deviations: The number of pictures is the script's num_pics_viewed250 (InfoGathering_Behaviour.m), and the pictures observed for measure (B) are the same ones. With the raw count of fixated pictures, (B) holds in both monkeys under readings (a), (c) and the script's, and in F only under (b); the value difference is then largest on 2-picture trials in F only.

outcomes.statement: On attribute trials, the free third saccade went preferentially to the option with the higher value between cue 1 and cue 2.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 3; Figure 2a
outcomes.quote: On ‘attribute’ trials, this saccade was preferentially directed towards the option with the higher relative expected value between cue 1 and cue 2
outcomes.notes: On attribute trials with a third picture, the logistic slope of returning to the first option on rank 1 minus rank 2 is 0.729 (F, p = 3.3e-190) and 1.210 (M, printed p = 0); the third saccade returns on 59.8% and 86.7% of trials when cue 1 outranks cue 2, against 8.7% and 10.0% otherwise.

outcomes.statement: On option trials, subjects sampled the fewest cues when cues 1 and 2 were highest in value and the most when they were lowest.
outcomes.source: Results, Experimental paradigm and subject behaviour, paragraph 3; Figure 2b
outcomes.quote: On ‘option’ trials, subjects sampled fewest pieces of information when cues 1 and 2 were highest in value, but most information when cues 1 and 2 were lowest in value
outcomes.notes: With both cues at rank +2, F sampled 2.05 and M 2.22 pictures, against 2.69 and 3.15 with both at -2; Spearman rho with the summed rank is -0.356 (F), -0.499 (M) and -0.434 (pooled), all p < 1e-143. The raw count gives the same direction.

outcomes.statement: At cue 1, DLPFC representational similarity reflects whether the subject is attending left or right; spatial attention is also represented in OFC and ACC.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraphs 4 and 5; Figure 4a-d
outcomes.quote: DLPFC RSA reflected whether the subject was attending left or right ( Fig. 4d ) ... for example, spatial attention is represented in both OFC and ACC ( Fig. 4d )
outcomes.notes: Spatial attention T = 39.90 in DLPFC (permutation p < 0.0001), 4.58 in OFC (p = 0.018) and 7.90 in ACC (p = 0.0028); CPD 80.2% in DLPFC against 13.7% (ACC) and 5.1% (OFC); F = 348.5, p < 0.0001. All four readings of O8 and O9 hold.

outcomes.statement: At cue 1, OFC representational similarity reflects the attended stimulus identity irrespective of its spatial position.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraph 4; Figure 4e
outcomes.quote: OFC representational similarity reflected the currently attended stimulus identity, irrespective of spatial position ( Fig. 4e )
outcomes.notes: Stimulus identity T = 14.82 in OFC (p < 0.0001), CPD 35.8% against 3.6% (ACC) and 4.9% (DLPFC); F = 23.8, p < 0.0001. All four readings hold.

outcomes.statement: At cue 1, OFC representational similarity is high for cues of similar attended value, consistent with a linear value code.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraphs 4 and 7; Figure 4a and 4f
outcomes.quote: OFC representational similarity reflected the currently attended stimulus identity, irrespective of spatial position ( Fig. 4e ), and was also high for cues of similar attended value ( Fig. 4f )
outcomes.notes: Attended value T = 5.86 in OFC (one-sided p = 0.0019, two-sided 0.0022), CPD 8.05% against 1.21% (ACC) and 0.14% (DLPFC); F = 4.84, p = 0.029. All four readings hold.

outcomes.statement: At cue 1, ACC and DLPFC representational similarity shows a value code modulated by whether the subject attends the left or right option.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraph 4; Figure 4g
outcomes.quote: ACC and DLPFC RSA showed a value code modulated by whether the subject was currently attending to the left or right option ( Fig. 4g )
outcomes.notes: Left/right value T = 6.05 in ACC (p = 0.0073) and 6.51 in DLPFC (p = 0.0036), 0.07 in OFC; CPD 8.5% and 9.7% against 0.0% in OFC. All four readings hold.

outcomes.statement: At cue 1, ACC representational similarity divides high-valued from low-valued cues, best explained as a categorical (accept/reject) function of value.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraphs 4 and 8; Figure 4c and 4h
outcomes.quote: ACC RSA also divided high-valued and low-valued items such that variance in ACC was best explained as a non-linear, categorical function of value ( Fig. 4h
outcomes.notes: Accept/reject T = 10.30 in ACC (p < 0.0001), CPD 21.3% against 4.7% in DLPFC; its CPD in ACC exceeds that of attended value (1.2%), reading (a). Attended value in ACC is not significant with all trials (one-sided p = 0.063) and is with 3 or more cues (p = 0.019), so reading (b) holds only with all trials. In OFC accept/reject has T = 8.71 and CPD 16.2%.

outcomes.statement: The triple dissociation of RSA matrices at cue 1 is consistent across the two monkeys.
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 2
outcomes.quote: This was consistent across subjects ( Fig. S2 )
outcomes.notes: All six coefficients are positive in each monkey under both trial readings (94, 37, 82 units in M and 95, 97, 101 in F); the smallest is 0.014 (left/right value in ACC of F, trials with 3 or more cues).

outcomes.statement: Split by top and bottom cue position (40 conditions), the RSA results replicate, and DLPFC similarity is also modulated by top/bottom position, so DLPFC represents spatial position more than left/right action.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 4 legend
outcomes.quote: in DLPFC, representational similarity is modulated by top/bottom stimulus location ... This indicates that DLPFC activity primarily represents spatial position
outcomes.notes: Same-quadrant minus same-side-other-row similarity is 0.112 in DLPFC, 0.042 in ACC and -0.001 in OFC. A label-permutation reference outside the criterion gives p < 0.001, 0.022 and 0.46.

outcomes.statement: Spatial attention reached 75% of its peak CPD at about the saccade (24, 72 and 67 ms in ACC, DLPFC, OFC); stimulus identity and attended value in OFC (269, 241 ms) and accept/reject (238 ms ACC, 224 ms OFC) followed; left/right value came later (457 ms ACC, 369 ms DLPFC).
outcomes.source: Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraph 6; Supplementary Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: Spatial attention affected representational similarity around the time of the saccadic eye-movement (t 75 =24ms in ACC, 72ms in DLPFC, 67ms in OFC) ... coding of stimulus identity and attended value (t 75 =269ms/241ms respectively in OFC) was comparable in latency to accept/reject coding (t 75 =238ms in ACC, 224ms in OFC). By contrast, action value coding emerged significantly later (t 75 =457ms in ACC, 369ms in DLPFC)
outcomes.notes: With a 10 ms step (reading a) all nine values are within tolerance over -100 to 500 ms (the measured values above). With a 1 ms step (reading b), as Fig4_RSA.m computes it, all nine equal the paper's (24, 72, 67, 269, 241, 238, 224, 457, 369 ms) over -200 to 600 ms; over -100 to 500 ms eight are equal and DLPFC left/right value is 358 ms (paper 369, within tolerance). Over -200 to 600 ms with a 10 ms step 8 of 9 are within tolerance (spatial attention in ACC 41 ms).

outcomes.statement: Spatial attention is encoded significantly earlier than stimulus identity, attended value and accept/reject, and left/right value (in ACC and DLPFC) significantly later than the other variables.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 5C legend; Results, Triply dissociable PFC population codes at first saccade, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: The distributions of t75 for spatial attention do not overlap with those of attended value, accept/reject, or stimulus identity, demonstrating that spatial attention is encoded significantly earlier than other variables. Similarly, left/right value (in ACC and DLPFC) is encoded significantly later than other variables.
outcomes.notes: The criterion's test fails under every reading. The t75 point estimates of the nine claimed curves follow the paper's order; with all the significant templates, in DLPFC accept/reject (491 ms) comes after left/right value (369 ms), while ACC (spatial attention 24, accept/reject 238, stimulus identity 262, left/right value 457 ms) and OFC (spatial attention 67, accept/reject 224, attended value 241, stimulus identity 269 ms) keep it. The 100 simulated t75 values overlap under both readings and with either set of variables (the criterion's significant templates, or the set Fig4_RSA.m stacks for the panel, peak CPD above 10%). In OFC the attended value range reaches -10 ms (reading a) and -13 ms (reading b), below the top of the spatial attention range (93 and 99 ms). In ACC left/right value (252 to 492 ms, reading a; 246 to 528 ms, reading b) overlaps accept/reject (229 to 272 ms; 227 to 291 ms). With the script's set, spatial attention lies below the other variables in ACC and DLPFC and left/right value above them in DLPFC, under both readings. The first run recorded partially_reproduced; it was changed after the first verification round, as its one test fails in at least two of the three regions under every reading. In figs1ab-cue-weights, which stays partially_reproduced, one component fails in one monkey and the rest holds.
deviations: Fig4_RSA.m draws one permutation of the residuals shared over time points (reading b) and computes t75 over -199 to 600 ms at 1 ms, as done here; it keeps the variables with peak CPD above 10% (Supplementary Figure 5B legend, "Regressors explaining little variance have been removed"), shown beside the criterion's significance rule.

outcomes.statement: Value encoding by OFC neurons peaked about 300 ms after each cue was revealed and stayed above baseline as further cues were attended.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 1; Figure 5a
outcomes.quote: This shows that value encoding by OFC neurons peaked approximately 300ms after each cue was revealed but was then sustained above baseline as further cues were attended.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a) the mean OFC CPD of cue 1, 2 and 3 value peaks 290, 300 and 290 ms after its own cue, and the cue 1 and cue 2 value CPDs are above either baseline at every bin of the later epochs (epoch means 0.18 to 0.52 points above). Reading (b) gives peaks of 290 to 320 ms and the same result.

outcomes.statement: In OFC, T-statistics for cue 1 value at cue 1 correlate positively across neurons with those for cue 2 value at cue 2, a stable subspace for the currently attended value.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 3; Figure 5b
outcomes.quote: we found that single neuron T-statistics for the regression of cue 1 value when cue 1 was attended (ordinate in Fig. 5b ) correlated positively with T-statistics for cue 2 value when cue 2 was attended (abscissa in Fig. 5b )
outcomes.notes: r = 0.845 (p = 7.7e-51, n = 182) with contrasts 19 and 20 (the script's), r = 0.843 with the mean T-statistics; M r = 0.860, F r = 0.809.
deviations: Unit 653 is dropped, as Fig5_OFCcrosscorrelation.m does (its T-statistics at cue 2 are not finite), so OFC has 182 units.

outcomes.statement: In OFC, at cue 2 of attribute trials, the attended cue 2 value subspace correlates negatively with the stored cue 1 value subspace (the other option).
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 4; Figure 5c
outcomes.quote: when cue 2 was attended on ‘attribute’ trials, the currently attended cue 2 value subspace correlated negatively with the stored cue 1 value subspace, representing the other option

outcomes.statement: In OFC, at cue 3 of option trials, the attended cue 3 value subspace correlates negatively with both the stored cue 1 and the stored cue 2 value subspaces.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 4; Figure 5d and 5e
outcomes.quote: when cue 3 was attended on ‘option’ trials, the stored cue 1 and stored cue 2 values both represented the other option and were both negatively correlated with currently attended cue 3 value subspace

outcomes.statement: In OFC, at cue 3 of option trials, the stored cue 1 and stored cue 2 value subspaces correlate positively, so the two previously attended cues are combined.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 4; Figure 5f
outcomes.quote: However, these two stored subspaces were themselves positively correlated at cue 3 on ‘option’ trials ( Fig. 5f ).
outcomes.notes: At cue 3 r = 0.523 (p = 3.4e-14); at cue 2 r = -0.033 (p = 0.66), as the Discussion says.

outcomes.statement: Cross-correlating the OFC value subspaces across time shows the same population subspace shifting its value encoding from positive to negative as the subject saccades around the screen.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 5; Figure 5g-j
outcomes.quote: This reveals how the same OFC population subspace would dynamically shift its encoding of values from positive to negative as the subject saccaded around the screen.
outcomes.notes: With each pair of cue epochs as its own 61 x 61 map and null, as the script computes them, the clusters through the 250 ms point have 884, 1839, 1105 and 817 bins against 99.9th-percentile thresholds of 442, 444, 453 and 487, with the signs of Figure 5c-f; EV 6 at cue 2 against EV 5 at cue 1 forms a positive cluster of 1622 bins (threshold 640, r = 0.755). With one 183 x 183 map over the cue 1, 2 and 3 epochs and a single null, the criterion also holds (1943, 6827, 1105 and 817 bins against 1414, 1056, 1083 and 810; EV 6 at cue 2 with EV 5 at cue 1, 5741 bins), with narrow margins for the two cue 3 option maps. That pass depends on the seed. With 10 other seeds the EV 3 with EV 2 cluster passes in 0 of 10 (thresholds 853 to 1262) and with 10000 permutations it fails (threshold 990); EV 3 with EV 1 passes in 7 of 10 and with 10000 permutations (984). So the single-map reading does not hold, and the outcome rests on the script's separate maps, which pass by wide margins.
deviations: The map pairs are those of Fig5_OFCcrosscorrelation.m (EV 6/5, 2/1, 3/1, 3/2); its correlation divides a population covariance by sample standard deviations, a factor of 181/182 on r, which is not reproduced here.

Each pair of epochs is its own map with its own null, as Fig5_OFCcrosscorrelation.m (lines 145-153 and 167) computes them; clusters are 8-connected, as bwconncomp in cross_corr_tstats.m. The single 183 x 183 map is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: The value comparison correlations of Figure 5c-e are stronger in OFC than in DLPFC (p = 0.040, 0.067, 0.011) and than in ACC (p = 0.003, 0.0003, 0.00013), by Fisher r-to-Z tests.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 6; Figure 5k
outcomes.quote: revealed significantly stronger population encoding in OFC than in DLPFC (attribute trials: VCue2 vs. VCue1, p = 0.040; option trials: VCue3 vs. VCue1, p = 0.067; VCue3 vs. VCue2, p = 0.011; Z-test after Fisher r-to-Z transformation) and in OFC than in ACC (attribute trials: VCue2 vs. VCue1, p = 0.003; option trials: VCue3 vs. VCue1, p = 0.0003; VCue3 vs. VCue2, p = 0.00013)

statistics.about: OFC against DLPFC, attribute trials, cue 2 value against cue 1 value
OFC against DLPFC, option trials, cue 3 value against cue 1 value
OFC against DLPFC, option trials, cue 3 value against cue 2 value
OFC against ACC, attribute trials, cue 2 value against cue 1 value
OFC against ACC, option trials, cue 3 value against cue 1 value
OFC against ACC, option trials, cue 3 value against cue 2 value

outcomes.notes: Two-sided Fisher tests (as the script) give p = 0.0397, 0.0670, 0.0108 against DLPFC and 0.0032, 0.0003 against ACC, the paper's values, and for EV 3 against EV 2 against ACC z = -4.357, p = 1.3e-05, ten times smaller than the paper's 0.00013; all six OFC correlations are more negative, five of six p < 0.05 (six of six one-sided). With units 87 and 653 put back (653 for the cue 3 correlations only, its cue 2 T-statistics not being finite) and the paper's n of 183, 135 and 189 in the test, all six are more negative and five of six have p < 0.05 (0.018, 0.067, 0.013 against DLPFC).
deviations: Units 87 (DLPFC) and 653 (OFC) are dropped, as Fig5_OFCcrosscorrelation.m does, so n is 182 OFC and 134 DLPFC units where the paper reports 183 and 135; the paper's n is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: ACC and DLPFC carry the currently attended value subspace (and stored subspaces) but show no negative correlation between attended and stored value subspaces.
outcomes.source: Results, Attention-guided value comparison in OFC, paragraph 6; Supplementary Figures 6 and 7
outcomes.quote: Whilst the currently attended value subspace was present in DLPFC and ACC, value comparison with stored cues was absent in these regions ( Fig 5k ; Figs. S6-7 ).
outcomes.notes: Presence holds in ACC (r = 0.852 and 0.559) and DLPFC (r = 0.658 and 0.519), all p < 1e-9. No attended-against-stored correlation is negative with p < 0.05 (ACC r = 0.031, 0.084, 0.058; DLPFC r = -0.040, -0.080, -0.105; smallest p 0.23).

outcomes.statement: In ACC the T-statistics of the four belief confirmation regressors (cues 2 and 3, option and attribute trials) correlate positively with each other and with cue 1 value, a stable belief confirmation code not present in OFC or DLPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Parallel ACC signals, paragraph 2; Figure 6a; Supplementary Figure 10
outcomes.quote: We found that ACC population subspaces for each of these regressors were significantly correlated with each other and also to cue 1 belief confirmation ( Fig. 6a / Fig. S10 ). As all five regressors are defined at different parts of the trial, this reveals a stable population code in ACC for accepting/rejecting the current belief, which was not present in OFC or DLPFC
outcomes.notes: With T-statistics all 10 ACC correlations are positive with p < 0.05 (r = 0.165 to 0.483), against 3 of 10 in DLPFC and 2 of 10 in OFC; with OLS coefficients ACC has 8 of 10. By monkey, ACC has 10 of 10 (M) and 7 of 10 (F).

outcomes.statement: Virtually all belief confirmation correlations are stronger in ACC than in OFC and DLPFC, and most of the individual comparisons are significant by Fisher r-to-Z.
outcomes.source: Results, Parallel ACC signals, paragraph 2; Figure 6b
outcomes.quote: Virtually all of these correlations were stronger in ACC than OFC/DLPFC ( Fig. 6b , right panels), and the majority of individual comparisons were significant ( Fig 6b , left panels).
outcomes.notes: The ACC correlation is larger in 19 of 20 comparisons; 13 of 20 have p < 0.05 two-sided (16 one-sided). With OLS coefficients 16 of 20 and 10 of 20.

outcomes.statement: ACC activity in the belief confirmation subspace separates short from long reaction time trials early in the trial, even at cue 1 presentation.
outcomes.source: Results, Parallel ACC signals, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 6c (Methods call the stimulus-locked panel 6B)
outcomes.quote: First, activity in this subspace separated short from long RT trials relatively early during the course of making a choice – even at the time of cue 1 presentation.
outcomes.notes: Under all 36 combinations of O4 to O7 (with the scripts' fixed RT bins added to O5, and the scripts' stored random halves and halves shared within a session as O4 readings b and c) the shortest RT bin is above the longest over 100-500 and 0-500 ms after cue 1 (odd/even, scripts' bins, Hz, mean T, a difference of 0.445); with 100 random halves it holds in 98 to 100 splits. The same holds in all 36 with the Methods' two-column projection and with the action weights at -200 ms (smallest difference 0.012). The data projected here equal those the scripts stored (av_Cue1L_proj and av_RespRT_LR_proj of info_gathering_ramp_to_choice.mat, read for the first five random halves) to within 1.4e-07 for every ACC unit, apart from the 1 cue-locked and 14 response-locked traces with a single trial, which the script stores as that trial's average over time. With the weights also matching the stored ones, the projections are those of the scripts up to that quirk.
deviations: The projection design is the scripts' (Fig6_ACCmultiplesignals_R3_version.m) [demeaned belief weights, demeaned action weights, constant, mean of EVs 11 and 12], and the action weights are taken at the bin the scripts index as 30 (centred 210 ms before the response). The Methods' projection on a neurons x 2 weight matrix (Projection of ACC activity) and the bin centred 200 ms before the response are run as variants.

O4 reading (b) uses the 100 random halves the scripts drew and stored (randproj_trials of info_gathering_cue123_alltrials_attentional_final.mat); the weights computed on them equal the stored weights to within 2.6e-07. Those halves are drawn per unit, so a unit's weight trials can be projected trials of a simultaneously recorded unit; reading (c) draws halves once per session, shared by its units.
The scripts' RT bins (below 1.2 s, 1.2-1.4, 1.4-1.6, 1.6-1.8, from 1.8 s) are run beside the claims file's quintile readings.
The traces are not cut at each bin's longest RT, which the script does for plotting; the windows used lie before those cuts.

outcomes.statement: Irrespective of reaction time, ACC activity in the belief confirmation subspace ramps up shortly before the joystick movement.
outcomes.source: Results, Parallel ACC signals, paragraph 4; Figure 6d (Methods call the response-locked panel 6C)
outcomes.quote: Second, irrespective of reaction time, ACC activity ramped shortly prior to joystick movement ( Fig. 6d ). Activity within the belief confirmation subspace therefore became prominent immediately prior to commitment to action, on all trials.
outcomes.notes: Under all 36 combinations the mean belief projection over -200 to 0 ms exceeds that over -500 to -300 ms in all five RT bins, and in all 36 with the Methods' two-column projection and with the action weights at -200 ms.
deviations: As fig6c; the response-locked trace averages the left- and right-choice projections, as the script does.

outcomes.statement: ACC activity in the left/right action selection subspace ramps up as evidence is revealed and peaks immediately before the response.
outcomes.source: Results, Parallel ACC signals, paragraph 5; Figure 6e (Methods call it 6D)
outcomes.quote: Activity in the ACC action selection subspace also gradually ramped as evidence was revealed about which option to choose, and peaked immediately prior to action selection ( Fig. 6e ).
outcomes.notes: The action projection rises over -500 to 0 ms in every RT bin under all 72 readings and all four combinations of projection design and action bin. With the scripts' design and bin its maximum over -500 to 100 ms lies between -200 and 100 ms in all five bins under 12 of 72 readings, among them the scripts' own (their stored halves, their RT bins, z-scored rates, mean T-statistics, left minus right); with the action weights at -200 ms under 16 of 72, and with the Methods' two-column projection under 6 of 72 at either bin. In the other readings one or two bins peak 10 to 60 ms before -200 ms (for example -240 ms in the longest bin, -260 ms in the fourth bin with quintiles per monkey and z-scored rates). The outcome follows the criterion's rule (one reading suffices) and rests on the peak window's lower edge.

outcomes.statement: At all three time points (cue 2 against cue 1, cue 3 against cue 1, cue 3 against cue 2), a greater proportion of single neurons encoded value difference between attended and unattended cues in OFC than in ACC and DLPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 2; Figure 7a
outcomes.quote: At all three relevant timepoints, we found that a greater proportion of single neurons passed these criteria in OFC than in ACC/DLPFC ( Fig. 7a ).
outcomes.notes: A reader's answer (questions/hunt-2018.yaml) amended the criterion, which had required OFC to lead at both p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, to require one reading of the significance level, and added the script's threshold |T| > 1.64 as reading (c). The first run gave partially_reproduced. The proportions are unchanged. With the Figure 5 trial types (reading a), OFC has the largest proportion at all three tests at 250 ms for p < 0.05 (OFC 6.0, 4.4, 6.6% against ACC 5.3, 3.2, 4.8% and DLPFC 1.5, 2.2, 2.2%), at 300 ms for p < 0.01 (1.6, 1.6, 3.3% against 1.1, 0.5, 1.1% and 1.5, 1.5, 1.5%), and with |T| > 1.64 at both bins. It fails at 250 ms for p < 0.01, at 300 ms for p < 0.05, and under the attribute-trial reading (b) in every combination. The differences are small; at 250 ms and p < 0.05 the smallest of the six pairwise chi-square p values is 0.084, and by monkey OFC leads at all three tests in M (6.2, 6.2, 8.6%) but not in F, where ACC is higher at both cue 3 tests (3.2 and 7.4% against OFC 3.0 and 5.0%).

outcomes.statement: Collapsed across the three tests, the fraction of neurons passing the value difference criteria at any of the three cues is greater in OFC than in ACC and DLPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 2; Figure 7b
outcomes.quote: We collapsed across these three tests to show the fraction of single neurons passing these criteria at any of the three cues individually ( Fig. 7b ).
outcomes.notes: With reading (a), OFC has the largest fraction passing any test at both bins and all thresholds (250 ms, p < 0.05 OFC 11.5%, ACC 9.0%, DLPFC 6.0%), so it holds under each reading with which fig7a now holds after the reader's answer on the significance level; the outcome is unchanged.

outcomes.statement: At all four time points, a greater proportion of single neurons significantly encoded belief confirmation in ACC than in OFC or DLPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 3; Figure 7c
outcomes.quote: At all four timepoints, there was a greater proportion of single neurons significantly encoding belief confirmation in ACC than in OFC or DLPFC ( Fig. 7c ).
outcomes.notes: ACC is highest for all four EVs at both bins and both thresholds (300 ms, p < 0.05 ACC 16.4, 20.1, 19.6, 11.1% against at most 10.4, 12.7, 8.2, 6.7%); in M alone DLPFC is higher for EV 13 (16.2% against 12.8%).

outcomes.statement: At cue 1, a significant fraction of neurons in all three regions encoded the cue's value irrespective of its attribute, action or spatial position.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 4; Figure 8
outcomes.quote: Across all three regions, a significant fraction of neurons encoded Cue 1’s value, irrespective of the cue’s attribute, action or spatial position ( Fig. 8 ; binomial test, all p<1*10 7 ).

statistics.n: 189 ACC, 135 DLPFC and 183 OFC neurons, each region tested

outcomes.notes: All 24 readings and the script's regression give binomial p < 1e-7 in every region (script ACC 54.0%, DLPFC 41.8%, OFC 59.0%), also with the exact binomial test. The script's regression gives the T-statistics stored in info_gathering_cue1_both.mat to within 3.3e-07; the significance flags the authors stored give 54.5%, 41.0% and 56.8%.
deviations: The script's own regression (InfoGathering_Neurons_Cue1_regression.m, 13 regressors on raw values, significance from 1000 trial permutations corrected over the bins from 0 to 500 ms) is run as a further reading.

outcomes.statement: About 18% of ACC and DLPFC neurons encoded left/right action value at cue 1, above chance and more than OFC, which encoded action value at chance level.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 5; Figure 8
outcomes.quote: First, a significant subset of ACC and DLPFC neurons (~18%) preferentially responded to the values of either left or right options (binomial test, both p<1*10 -5 ). Both of these populations were significantly greater than OFC, which encoded action value at chance level (pairwise Chi 2 test, ACC vs. OFC: p=0.002, DLPFC vs. OFC: p=0.003).

statistics.about: ACC and DLPFC action value fractions against chance

outcomes.notes: The first reading the criterion lists (full model, 100-500 ms, all trials, p < 0.05) gives 19.0% and 18.7%, within tolerance, but OFC is above chance there (10.4%, p = 0.0018). The tests all hold in six readings and in the script's (ACC 20.6%, DLPFC 17.9%, binomial p = 2e-14 and 3e-08, chi-square against OFC p = 6.8e-05 and 0.0016, OFC 6.0%, p = 0.41), in none of them with both fractions within 18 +/- 1.8%. With the exact binomial test the tests hold in five readings and the script's; reading (b, iii, b, p < 0.05) fails it (DLPFC exact p = 1e-05), and none has both fractions within tolerance. The significance flags the authors stored (info_gathering_cue1_both.mat, from the same regression, whose T-statistics match these to 3.3e-07, with their own permutations) give ACC 18.5% and DLPFC 17.2% with every test holding. They differ from the flags computed here in 2.1% of ACC units, so the gap is permutation noise around the threshold, but those flags are the paper's result and not one computed here, so the outcome is not changed on them.

outcomes.statement: In DLPFC, top/bottom spatial value neurons are as prevalent as left/right action value neurons, while in ACC they are significantly fewer, so DLPFC encodes value by spatial position and ACC by action.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 6; Figure 8
outcomes.quote: In DLPFC, such a relationship held: an equally prevalent population of top-bottom ‘spatial value’ neurons was observed as left-right ‘action value’ neurons (binomial test, p<1*10 -6 ). In ACC, this population was significantly smaller than the left-right value population (pairwise Chi 2 test p=0.03).

statistics.about: DLPFC spatial value fraction against chance
ACC spatial value against action value fractions

outcomes.notes: Holds under 2 of 24 readings (100-500 ms, all trials, p < 0.01, either model); with the full model DLPFC spatial value 8.2% (binomial p = 3e-08) against action value 7.5% (chi-square p = 1), ACC 2.6% against 13.2% (p = 0.0003). In the script's reading DLPFC spatial is 15.7% against 17.9% (p = 0.74) and ACC 9.0% against 20.6% (p = 0.0024), but the DLPFC binomial p is 2e-06, above the 1e-6 bound; the authors' stored flags give the same (7e-06). With the exact binomial test the full-model reading still holds (p = 1e-07) and the value-only one does not (1e-06). In both passing readings the DLPFC action fraction is 7.5 to 9.0%, against the about 18% of the sibling claim. The outcome follows the criterion's rule (one reading suffices).

outcomes.statement: About 24% of OFC neurons encoded attribute value at cue 1 (preferring probability or magnitude cues), above chance and more than in ACC or DLPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Single neuron analyses recapitulate core findings at population level, paragraph 7; Figure 8
outcomes.quote: we found a significant proportion of neurons in OFC (~24%) reflected attribute value (binomial test, p<1*10 7 ) ... This proportion was significantly greater than the representation of attribute value coding in either ACC or DLPFC (pairwise Chi 2 tests, OFC vs. ACC: p=0.001, OFC vs. DLPFC: p=0.014).

statistics.about: OFC attribute value fraction against chance

outcomes.notes: The first reading gives 26.2% of OFC (binomial p = 4e-22), above ACC (5.8%, chi-square p = 1.6e-07) and DLPFC (11.9%, p = 0.0028); the script's reading gives 23.0% (p = 3e-17), above ACC (7.9%, p = 0.00011) and DLPFC (11.2%, p = 0.011). The exact binomial test gives the same outcomes, and the authors' stored flags give 23.5%.

outcomes.statement: The GLM's regressors of interest are decorrelated by design except EV 16, whose mean r2 with EVs 7 and 9 is 0.167 and 0.194.
outcomes.source: Online Methods, General linear model, EV 16 paragraph; Supplementary Figure 9
outcomes.quote: there existed some positive correlation between EV16 and EVs 7 and 9 (mean r 2 of 0.167 and 0.194 respectively, see Figure S9 )
outcomes.notes: Over neurons on trials with 3 or more cues (reading b) the mean r2 is 0.180 (EV 7) and 0.190 (EV 9), and the largest other pair among EVs 1-6 and 13-18 is 0.046 (EV 2 with EV 13). Over sessions (reading a) 0.190 and 0.204, the first outside tolerance. The script computes the matrix on all trials (0.180 and 0.198 over neurons).

outcomes.statement: Replacing the attended value and left/right value templates by a uniform-diagonal form (negative absolute value difference) gives qualitatively the same functional dissociation across OFC, DLPFC and ACC.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Note, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 11
outcomes.quote: such a regressor to analyse the data in main Figure 4 yields a similar functional dissociation between OFC, DLPFC and ACC for ‘attended value’ and ‘left/right value’
outcomes.notes: Attended value in OFC T = 3.31 (one-sided p = 0.0021) with CPD 2.72% against 0.37% and 0.29%; left/right value T = 6.75 (ACC) and 6.56 (DLPFC), -0.01 in OFC. Both fig4f and fig4g criteria hold under all four readings.
deviations: The alternative template is the commented line of Fig4_RSA.m, -|rank(i) - rank(j)| demeaned.

findings.statement: Units are selected by the average_firing_rate field of other_data/all_units_info.mat, which the paper's scripts use for the 1 Hz exclusion. How it was computed is not documented, and it is neither the whole-session rate (the stored men) nor the rate over the analysed trials; those select 190, 136 and 182 or 186, 137 and 179 units in ACC, DLPFC and OFC, where the field gives the paper's 189, 135 and 183.
The unit files 681 to 724 (sessions 5, 11, 23 and 27 of Miles) store the subject letter sb as lower case "m", while all other units of Miles store "M".

The data descriptor, the README and the scripts' flowchart name the preprocessed units neuronal_data/LTH_preprocessed_data, but the archive holds them as neuronal_data/LTH_processed_data.zip, the folder name the scripts read.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module pfc7.py and the claims file, with the paper's full text and supplement under paper/. The verifier tested helpers on synthetic inputs (conv_same_200, ols, cpd, chi2_yates, fisher_z, t75, the RSA templates and the GLM bins) and compared the archive's S3 listing with the files the notebook reads. It did not download the data set, so it could not read the scripts in scripts.zip. Its remaining points, answered in the record, are that statements about the scripts should be printed in the notebook (now done in the data check), that conv_same_200 is shifted by one sample from numpy's same (it follows MATLAB's conv2 same, which keeps one sample later for an even kernel; the docstring now says so), and that info_gathering_ramp_to_choice.mat (5.3 GB) could validate Figure 6 (not read, as a 5.3 GB MATLAB file is beyond what the run streams into memory; the stored random halves and weights of info_gathering_cue123_alltrials_attentional_final.mat validate the Figure 6 weights instead, and no stored RSA output exists in the data set).

disagreements.reason: Cell 54 shows it fails under both residual readings and both variable sets. In ACC the left/right value range (252 to 492) overlaps accept/reject (229 to 272). In OFC the spatial attention range (13 to 93/99) overlaps attended value (-10/-13 to 286/367).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the revision after round 1, with the conclusion cells and the summary, the helper module pfc7.py, the attempt record, the README and the claims file, with the paper under paper/. The verifier agreed with every outcome and checked the round-1 reasons restated in the record. Its point that the Summary table shows outcomes resting on a minority of readings as plain reproduced is answered by marking them in the table and the README.

paper_notes.statement: Every figure script drops unit 87 (DLPFC, 4.8 Hz) as a bad cell, and the Figure 5 and 7 scripts also drop unit 653 (OFC, whose cue 2 T-statistics are not finite), so the DLPFC analyses use 134 units and the OFC analyses of Figures 5 and 7 use 182, where the paper reports 135 and 183 (for example n = 135 DLPFC units in the Supplementary Figure 5 legend). The paper does not mention these exclusions.

For Figure 7a the Results say the cue 3 tests were made "at cue 3 of attribute trials" while citing Figure 5d/e, which are option trials; the script (Fig7_single_neurons_cue2and3.m) tests EV 3 against EVs 1 and 2, the option-trial regressors.

The Methods for Figure 6 describe a neurons x 2 projection matrix from odd and even trials, with weights for action 200 ms before the response. The published script (Fig6_ACCmultiplesignals_R3_version.m) averages 100 random half splits, adds a constant and the mean option/attribute response to the projection design, takes the action weights at the bin centred 210 ms before the response, and uses fixed reaction-time bins (below 1.2 s, 1.2-1.4, 1.4-1.6, 1.6-1.8, from 1.8 s) that the Methods do not give.

Two thresholds of the single-neuron analyses are not in the text. Figure 7 counts a neuron as encoding value difference when each of three T-statistics exceeds 1.64 in absolute value (Fig7_single_neurons_cue2and3.m), and belief confirmation at 1.96, and Supplementary Figure 1c judges accuracy on the pictures seen, averaged over sessions (InfoGathering_Behaviour.m); the results here depend on both choices (fig7a, figs1cd). The authors could confirm that these are the choices behind the figures.

The paper does not define when a cue counts as "evaluated" in "subjects chose before all four cues had been evaluated on 85.5%/71.4% of trials". The script's count, corrected for a joystick movement made before the last fixation (InfoGathering_Behaviour.m, out.earlychoices), gives 85.52% and 71.43%; the count of fixated pictures gives 54.23% and 42.56%, and pictures fixated for more than 250 ms 95.59% and 92.25%. The authors could confirm that the script's count is the one behind the reported numbers.

The caption of Supplementary Table 1 says it gives the units with average firing rate above 1 Hz in each session, but its counts are those of all units. They agree with the data set's units in all 53 sessions and three areas when every unit is counted, and in 26 of 53 when units below 1 Hz are left out, and they sum to 198 ACC, 156 DLPFC and 195 OFC units, against the 189, 135 and 183 the text reports after the 1 Hz exclusion.

InfoGathering_Neurons_Ramp_to_choice.m averages each reaction-time bin with MATLAB's mean over the selected rows, which for a selection of one trial averages over time, so a bin holding a single trial is stored as a flat line at that trial's mean in info_gathering_ramp_to_choice.mat. In the first five random halves this affects 1 cue-locked and 14 response-locked traces of ACC units out of several thousand; every other trace matches the data computed here to within 1.4e-07.

entries.name: hunt-2018
entries.title: Attention and decision computations across prefrontal cortex (Hunt, Malalasekera et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Hunt, Malalasekera et al. (2018) on CRCNS data set pfc-7, which holds the behaviour of two macaques in an information sampling task and single units from ACC, DLPFC and OFC. It covers the behaviour, the representational similarity analysis at cue 1, the value comparison subspaces in OFC, the belief confirmation and action subspaces in ACC, and the single-neuron analyses, all from the data set's preprocessed units and behavioural files.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hunt, Malalasekera et al. (2018) from CRCNS pfc-7

papers.title: Triple dissociation of attention and decision computations across prefrontal cortex
